correctness.rationale: At fixed n the inverse-average-degree proxy ranks only by edge count; the inverse-adjacency-spectral proxy ranks by Perron root. I independently generated ALL connected unlabeled simple graphs for n=2,3,4,5 (1,2,6,21 classes, respectively), computed exact characteristic polynomials and rational real-root isolating intervals, and compared each class pair with unequal edge counts. All n<=5 edge-rank orders were spectral-radius nondecreasing: zero strict reversal pairs. Symbolically K_{1,5} has 5 edges, mean degree 5/3, Perron root sqrt(5)>2, while C6 has 6 edges, mean 2 and Perron root 2. For all n>=6, n-1<n and sqrt(n-1)>2 ensure the same strict reversal. This is complete finite proof of minimality plus exact infinite family; neither numerical approximations nor finite checks support the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The precise first connected equal-order network size at which two widely-used epidemic vulnerability proxies induce opposite strict ranks is a motivated exact finite boundary. It quantifies a failure mode with a rigorous minimum and establishes persistence on a natural infinite graph family; the result does not assert true finite stochastic SIS extinction thresholds.
